2609.09848.title: Subgroup Membership Inference Audits of Differentially Private Synthetic Text
2609.09848.paper_summary: Synthetic data releases are increasingly proposed in the literature as a means of sharing realistic data replicas in lieu of sensitive private datasets. Even when the worst-case privacy leakage of such releases is bounded by means of differential privacy (DP), in practice a residual risk remains. Membership inference attack (MIA) audits are conducted to empirically quantify this risk. However, existing methods only measure average-case risk for randomly drawn records, which might conceal the risk to vulnerable subgroups. To highlight this issue, we define a subgroup-targeted membership inference game in which the target pool is an explicit parameter, and instantiate it with an audit of 32 proxies under three scenarios with different levels of attacker knowledge, across four datasets, three generators (DP-SGD fine-tuning, API-based prompting, and activation steering), and five privacy budgets. The audit shows that synthetic releases leak subgroup membership and that prior attacks systematically underestimate this leakage. DP is effective at the aggregate level: it substantially reduces average leakage at every budget we test. Three observations temper this picture. First, the remaining leakage is concentrated rather than spread out: under DP, a tenth of the records carries roughly 40% of it. Second, the protection DP delivers in practice is uneven: within its worst-case guarantee, the noise removes more of the measured leakage from random records than from high-risk ones---and a merged-pool audit that scores both record types against shared negatives confirms this at the record level. Third, \emph{which} records leak proves to be a property of the release mechanism rather than of the record alone, so record-level risk cannot be assessed independently of the release.
2609.09848.paper_summary_zh: 合成數據發布在文獻中越來越多地被提議作為分享現實數據複製品的手段，以取代敏感的私有數據集。即使這些發布的最壞情況隱私洩漏是通過差分隱私（DP）來界定的，實際上仍然存在殘餘風險。進行成員推斷攻擊（MIA）審計以實證量化這一風險。然而，現有方法僅測量隨機抽取記錄的平均情況風險，這可能掩蓋對脆弱子群體的風險。為了突出這一問題，我們定義了一個針對子群體的成員推斷遊戲，其中目標池是一個明確的參數，並在三種不同攻擊者知識水平的情境下，對32個代理進行審計，涵蓋四個數據集、三個生成器（DP-SGD微調、基於API的提示和激活引導）以及五個隱私預算。審計顯示合成發布洩漏了子群體成員資格，並且之前的攻擊系統性地低估了這種洩漏。DP在整體層面上是有效的：它在我們測試的每個預算中顯著減少了平均洩漏。三個觀察結果緩和了這一情況。首先，剩餘的洩漏是集中而非分散的：在DP下，十分之一的記錄大約承擔了40%的洩漏。其次，DP在實際中提供的保護是不均勻的：在其最壞情況的保證下，噪聲從隨機記錄中去除的洩漏量多於從高風險記錄中去除的量——而一個合併池審計在記錄層面確認了這一點，對兩種類型的記錄進行了共享負面評分。第三，\emph{哪些}記錄洩漏被證明是發布機制的特性，而不是記錄本身的特性，因此記錄層面的風險無法獨立於發布進行評估。
